title: UniPoolerV2 'The zap' NatSpec and story-051 misstate the donation mechanism and beneficiary: an unsynced donation was never 'absorbed into our swap and LP mint' and does not accrue 'overwhelmingly' to this contract's POL by code guarantee
storyTag: story-051 (review/); related to L-25 8ec2be7d59 NatSpec half of the fix plan
description: Without a sync, the router fixes amountOut from the stale reserves. The donation only enlarges swap()'s computed amountIn, which loosens the K check, and swap()'s _update() then folds it into the reserves. The pooler receives nothing extra from the swap or the mint. The stranding comes from the router's _addLiquidity quoting against the shifted post-swap reserves while s was sized on the stale ones. In both cases (unsynced pre-fix, and synced post-fix) the donation accrues pro-rata to the LP holders that existed before our mint. Because mainnet V2 feeTo is ON (0xf385...5f85) and sync() does not touch kLast, feeTo also takes about 1/6 of the sqrt(k) growth the donation causes at the next mint/burn, our own addLiquidity included. 'Overwhelmingly this contract's POL' holds only to the extent that UniPoolerV2 holds the pre-existing LP. The cutover seed LP recipient is set by the phStaging2 script, not this contract.
impact: None from the code. The NatSpec mis-describes who benefits from an unsynced donation. The code behaves correctly: sync() folds the donation into reserves pro rata to all LPs. The pooler's LP mint never captures the donation, and feeTo later takes about 1/6 of the resulting sqrt(k) growth.
likelihood: Low that an operator makes an unsafe decision from this text (see justification).
assumptions: POL share of the pair is not guaranteed by code; it is an operational fact that can change if third parties LP
severityJustification: 'The zap' NatSpec says an unsynced donation 'would be absorbed into our swap and LP mint', and that syncing gives it 'to the pair's LPs, overwhelmingly this contract's POL'. Both statements are imprecise. In V2, the router fixes amountOut from reserves, so a donation present at swap() only eases the k-check. It is then folded into reserves by swap()'s _update and accrues pro rata to every LP. It never enters our LP mint. 'Overwhelmingly POL' is a market-structure observation, not a code guarantee, and since feeTo is live (Q-23), about 1/6 of the k growth is diverted at the next mint/burn. I checked whether an operator could make an unsafe decision from this text. None of the decisions the text informs are unsafe. Keeping sync() and never calling skim() is correct whoever the beneficiary is. The only decision the misstatement could distort is a knowing, voluntary protocol transfer of value directly into the pair in the expectation of capturing it. Under the externally-derived-value principle, that would at worst be a misallocation of the protocol's own gift (leakage = non-POL LP share + feeTo cut), not an attacker-reachable value leak. No code path in UniPoolerV2 or the dispatch flow sends tokens to the pair outside swap/addLiquidity. A non-malicious owner would not lose funds to an adversary through this. It is a documentation-faithfulness defect introduced by L-25's NatSpec rewrite and does not affect the FIX-COMPLETE verdict on L-25's code. Report it as F-02-051 at informational severity, visible to the owner.
recommendation: Rewrite the paragraph: 'without a sync, swap() folds the donation into reserves (pro rata to all LPs, less feeTo's protocol-fee share at the next mint/burn) while s, sized from stale reserves, no longer balances the legs'. Drop 'overwhelmingly this contract's POL' or mark it as an operational observation. Optionally correct the L-25 ledger title wording ('absorbed in swap()'). That edit is human-only.
specText: NatSpec :56-59: "V2 `swap()` credits the input as `balance - reserve`, so tokens transferred to the pair without a sync (a donation) would be absorbed into our swap and LP mint"; :60-62: "Syncing folds the donation into the reserves — to the pair's LPs, overwhelmingly this contract's POL". story-051 Background: "any unsynced balance in the pair is credited to our swap/mint by the real pair maths"; Implementation Notes: "(to the LPs, overwhelmingly the protocol)"
